stemMd:
What is the length of a train moving at constant speed?

(1) It takes 20 seconds for the entire train to pass a fixed pole.

(2) Its speed is 18 metres per second.

Which assessment of sufficiency is correct?

options.label: A
options.textMd: Even together the statements are not sufficient.

options.label: B
options.textMd: Together the statements are sufficient, but neither is sufficient alone.

options.label: C
options.textMd: Statement (1) alone is sufficient, but statement (2) alone is not.

options.label: D
options.textMd: Statement (2) alone is sufficient, but statement (1) alone is not.

explanationMd: Passing a pole requires travelling one train length. Time alone and speed alone do not determine distance. Together length is speed times time, 18 times 20 = 360 metres.

distractorRationale.c: Assess each statement separately before combining them. Passing a pole requires travelling one train length. Time alone and speed alone do not determine distance. Together length is speed times time, 18 times 20 = 360 metres.
